comparison: Perfect alignment on LDHA biomarker findings (C19-C22). Both evaluations support the identification of LDHA through immunofluorescence, TCGA analysis, and prognostic correlation. Peer reviewers did not challenge these findings and described the study as 'significantly improved.'

Complete agreement on metabolic shift findings (C23-C25). Both support the scMetabolism analysis showing stage-specific patterns. OpenEval notes functional significance requires further investigation, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as part of the 'comprehensive characterisation.'

Full concordance on human validation (C79-C91). Both strongly support the translation of mouse findings to human samples. Peer Reviewer 3 specifically highlighted this as a strength, and OpenEval notes this cross-species validation substantially strengthens conclusions.

Strong agreement on metabolic context and cell-cell interactions (C12-C18). OpenEval notes computational predictions require experimental validation, while Peer Reviewer 3 specifically praised the 'characterisation of cross-talk between macrophages and the lung precancerous cells' as a strength.

Agreement on background/contextual claims (C92-C95). Both support these literature-based assertions. OpenEval validates through citations, peer reviewers did not question the biological rationale or mouse model appropriateness.

Strong alignment on S100a4+ macrophage identification (C26-C32). This is the core finding. Editor described it as 'important,' and Reviewer 2 specifically noted the demonstration of S100a4+ alveolar macrophages active in fatty acid metabolism. OpenEval supports the convergent characterization through multiple analytical approaches. Peer result also includes histological validation claims (C33-C34, C36-C37) not in OpenEval R6.

Agreement on literature context claims (C96-C108 and related). Both support these citation-based contextual claims. Peer Reviewer 3 requested broader discussion of anti-macrophage therapies, which was adequately addressed. OpenEval notes these frame significance but are not novel discoveries.

Strong concordance on in vitro functional validation (C49-C59). Peer Reviewer 3 specifically praised 'functional validation of the effects of S100a4+ cells' as a strength. OpenEval supports the multiple complementary assays. Peer result also includes secretome characterization (C60-C63) not in OpenEval R10.

Alignment on metabolic-functional relationships (C42-C48). OpenEval notes correlations are statistically significant but don't establish causation. Peer reviewers support the findings, with Reviewer 3 previously requesting careful assessment of angiogenesis assumptions, which was adequately addressed. Peer result also includes functional phenotype claims (C38-C41) not in OpenEval R9.

Agreement on CPT1A inhibition experiments (C73-C78). OpenEval supports the pharmacological validation with etomoxir showing reversal of pro-tumorigenic effects. Peer Reviewer 3 praised functional validation as a strength. Peer result also includes flow cytometry and angiogenesis assays (C65-C69, C72) not in OpenEval R13.

Partial overlap on heterogeneity findings (C9-C10). Both support these claims. OpenEval notes the inference remains correlative rather than mechanistic. Peer reviewers described the study as 'convincing' with concerns 'adequately addressed.'

Agreement on functional phenotype characterization (C38-C41). OpenEval notes these are computational predictions rather than direct functional assays. Peer reviewers support the angiogenesis findings, with the editor noting 'a role in angiogenesis' as an important contribution. Peer result also includes metabolic-functional correlations (C42-C44, C46-C48) not in OpenEval R8.

Agreement on flow cytometry and angiogenesis validation (C65-C69, C72). OpenEval supports the ANXA2-PLG axis as plausible mechanism for angiogenesis, though notes direct functional testing needed. Peer reviewers accepted the mechanistic data as part of functional validation. Peer result also includes CPT1A inhibition experiments (C73-C78) not in OpenEval R12.

Partial agreement on mouse model foundation (C3-C5). Both support experimental procedures and histological validation. OpenEval R1 also includes model selection and citation support (C1-C2) not in peer R1. Peer R1 includes scRNA-seq quality metrics (C6-C8) not in OpenEval R1.

Partial overlap on histological validation (C33-C34, C36-C37). OpenEval R7 focuses on multiplex immunohistochemistry validation of triple-positive population and CPT1A function. Peer R6 covers broader S100a4+ macrophage characterization including scRNA-seq analysis (C26-C32) not in OpenEval R7.

Partial overlap on secretome characterization (C60-C63). OpenEval supports the pro-tumor phenotype evidence from western blotting and cytokine array. Peer R8 focuses more broadly on functional validation including coculture assays (C49-C59) not in OpenEval R11.

Minimal overlap on mouse model selection (C1-C2). Both support the use of A/J mice through citations. OpenEval R1 covers broader experimental foundation (C3-C5), while peer R11 focuses on background/contextual claims (C92-C95).

Partial overlap on scRNA-seq atlas generation (C6-C8). Both support the quality metrics and clustering. OpenEval R2 also includes heterogeneity analysis (C9-C10) not in peer R1. Peer R1 also covers experimental procedures (C3-C5) not in OpenEval R2.
